title: Universal Cell Embedding (UCE): Zero-Shot Cross-Species Foundation Model for Cell Biology
aiSystem: Universal Cell Embedding / UCE (Stanford / CZ Biohub / Arc Institute)
whyItMatters: Published in Nature, UCE maps ~36M cells across 8 species into a shared protein-grounded representation space, enabling zero-shot cell-type discovery and atlas integration across entirely unseen species.
summary: Published in Nature on July 8, 2026 (Vol. 656, Issue 8126, pp. 183–191, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10689-z, PMID 42420460), Yanay Rosen, Yusuf Roohani, Stephen Quake, Jure Leskovec, and collaborators at Stanford University, the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, and the Arc Institute introduced Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), a foundation model for single-cell biology. Rather than tying tokens to a single species’ gene vocabulary, UCE encodes each expressed gene using protein language model embeddings alongside chromosomal coordinates across ~36 million cells spanning eight diverse species. This species-agnostic representation allows UCE to embed cells from completely unseen organisms zero-shot without fine-tuning, align homologous cell types across hundreds of millions of years of evolution, and uncover novel cell-state relationships across disparate tissues and experimental batches.
technicalHighlights: Trained on ~36 million single-cell transcriptomes across 8 species using protein-language-model gene representations, eliminating fixed single-species gene vocabularies.
Embeds single-cell datasets from entirely unseen species zero-shot without retraining, accurately aligning conserved and divergent cell types across evolution.
Published in Nature (Vol. 656, PMC13441871) as a foundational representation layer for virtual-cell atlases and cross-species comparative biology.
caveats: Captures static single-cell transcriptomic states rather than causal perturbation dynamics or spatial tissue architecture on its own.

scoreRationale.foundational: Solves cross-species single-cell alignment by grounding gene identity in universal protein sequence embeddings rather than species-specific gene IDs.
scoreRationale.ripple: Enables zero-shot annotation of newly sequenced non-model organisms and unifies disparate cell atlases across biomedicine.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature with extensive zero-shot cross-species, batch-integration, and cell-ontology validation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Eliminates custom ortholog mapping and per-dataset retraining when analyzing newly profiled tissues or species.
